proof:
For two distinct points of $P$ in the same coset modulo $2L$, their midpoint belongs to $\Lambda$ and to $\operatorname{conv}(P)$, hence to $P$. Thus the occupied labels, positive masses and finite support satisfy the hypotheses of accepted fact `f4547c4166b39683`. Its halfspace depth is exactly $D_p$ in the comparison theorem. It yields $p\in P$ with $D_p\ge M/k$, and at such a point $E_p\ge T_p\ge D_p$. Outside the stated equal-vertex exception the accepted fact chooses the same $p$ with $M_p>M/k$. If $E_p>T_p$, then $E_p>M/k$. If $E_p=T_p$, the pointwise equality criterion gives $E_p=M_p>M/k$. In the exception every minimal face is a singleton, whose energy is the corresponding mass $M/k$. This also covers rank zero.

The quotient $L/2L$ has $2^{\operatorname{rank} L}$ elements, giving the stated weaker bound and its equality condition. The Boolean cube is lattice-complete, all its vertices occupy distinct parities, and every vertex face is a singleton.

Without completeness the lower bound can fail. For the five unit-mass points $(0,0),(2,0),(3,1),(1,3),(0,2)$ the cyclic turns are strictly positive and the polygon is convex, as is also seen from the five supporting lines $y=0$, $y=x-2$, $x+y=4$, $y=x+2$, and $x=0$. Each consecutive edge is exposed by its line with the other three points strictly on the same side. Hence each listed point is a vertex, so every energy is $1$, whereas $M/4=5/4$. The hull contains the omitted lattice point $(1,0)$.
statement:
Let $\Lambda=c+L$ be an affine lattice, and let $P$ be a nonempty finite set with $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\Lambda$. Give every $z\in P$ mass $m_z>0$, put $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$, and let $k$ be the number of occupied cosets modulo $2L$. For $N>0$ let $E_p$ be the power-entropy energy defined in the face-attainment result, using the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}(P)$ at each $p\in P$. Then
$$
\max_{p\in P}E_p\ge M/k,\qquad
\max_{p\in P}E_p=M/k
\ \Longleftrightarrow\
P\text{ consists of exactly }k\text{ vertices, all with mass }M/k.
$$
If $\operatorname{rank}L\le n$, the maximum is at least $M/2^n$, with equality exactly when $k=2^n$ and the same equal-vertex condition holds. Equal masses on $\{0,1\}^n$ attain this bound.
title: Equality in the occupied-parity power-entropy bound
